query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 2 wt% TiC nanoparticles to the Al0.5CrFeCoNi high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical capability by 20% at 1000°C and 500 MPa, while limiting density to less than 5% increase and preserving room-temperature performance to less than 10% decrease in yield strength, due to the formation of a stable oxide layer and dispersion of TiC nanoparticles.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable oxide layer and dispersion of TiC nanoparticles
generation.mechanism: The TiC nanoparticles act as nucleation sites for the formation of a stable oxide layer, which improves the high-temperature oxidation resistance and reduces the density of the alloy. The dispersion of TiC nanoparticles also enhances the strength and toughness of the alloy at room temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature mechanical capability (20% increase in yield strength at 1000°C) while limiting density (less than 5% increase) and preserving room-temperature performance (less than 10% decrease in yield strength at room temperature)
generation.baseline: Al0.5CrFeCoNi high-entropy alloy without TiC nanoparticles
generation.uncertainty: The uncertainty lies in the lack of prior studies investigating the effect of TiC nanoparticle addition on high-temperature mechanical capability in this specific alloy system.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength at 1000°C and 500 MPa does not increase by at least 15%, or if the density increases by more than 5%, the hypothesis is falsified.
